score: 681/720 schema-change scenarios answered exactly, 0 wrong, 39 declined as unknown (360 dev, 360 held out)
metric: Add, drop, rename or retype a column on a table in a generated pipeline; every downstream model must be reported as breaking, as changing its output columns or types, or as unaffected, matching an answer key computed by a simulator that never parses SQL.
correctness: 0 models that break or change output reported as safe; 0 false breaks; 0 unparsed models that mention the table reported as safe
held_out: First scored run of the held-out families (474 models): 2 models missed, both a SELECT * EXCEPT (col) or REPLACE over a column that was dropped, which BigQuery rejects and sqlglot ignores. Fixed afterwards, so those families no longer count as held out. Dev runs before it also exposed a bug that dropped table aliases, which made joins look unresolvable; reported then as unknown, never as safe.
caveats: Retypes are checked only where the type reaches an output column; an operation that is invalid on the new type is not detected. A retype feeding a UNION ALL of two SELECT * arms is scored against the numeric supertypes (INT64 < NUMERIC < FLOAT64) but no other set operation or supertype is generated, and those scenarios were added after the GoogleSQL type checker was hooked in, so they are not held out from it. Answers come from the generator, whose families are ones the tool's author could think of.
analysis: Breaks: precision 1.000, recall 1.000. Output changes: precision 1.000, recall 1.000. Exact columns added/removed/retyped: 460/460. Unparsed models are reported unknown (39 model answers).
performance: 15 ms per scenario on pipelines of 8 to 120 models
